2. Santavihārādhigama - The wisdom of attaining Arahatta-phala samāpatti (fruition attainment of Arahantship)

ayyamitta: [Ayya+mitta]  CL=7 A thera named Ayyamitta lived in the Kassaka Cave. A laywoman who lived in the alms village supported and took care of Ayyamitta Thera as her own son. One day, before she went to the forest, she told her daughter to cook almsfood with milk and ghee and to offer it to Ayyamitta Thera. As for herself, she had already eaten coarse rice and palm sap, so she asked her daughter to cook porridge made of broken rice mixed with vegetables for her midday meal. At that time, Ayyamitta Thera arrived and overheard her conversation. He reflected to himself: “This laywoman eats only coarse rice, palm sap, and porridge, while she prepares fine rice and ghee for me. She gives in this way not wishing for fields or farms, but wishing for the three kinds of sampatti. Am I capable of granting her those? Therefore, it is not proper to eat this alms while lust and anger remain in me.” Thus admonishing himself, he returned to the Kassaka Cave and made a firm resolution that he would not leave the cave unless he attained arahattaphala. Meditating in the cave, he attained arahattaphala by the morning and became an arahant. The deva dwelling at the cave entrance joyfully uttered an exclamation beginning with “Namo te purisājañña,” saying that laywomen who offer alms to such an arahant will be freed from the suffering of saṃsāra. As it was still early, Ayyamitta Thera went on almsround. The laywoman’s daughter offered him alms, and he expressed his appreciation by saying, “Sukhaṃ hotu,” and returned. At that time, the Thera’s bodily appearance was clear and radiant. When the laywoman returned and heard the full account from her daughter, she understood that the Thera had completed his holy task and said, “Your brother truly delights in the Dispensation now; he is no longer weary.” See: Mahāmitta Thera.
